answer: A new identity may claim rewards only after three established agents cite its graded work inside their own graded work. Each citation puts the citer's standing and pending rewards at risk if the cited work proves fake. A trellis holds a new shoot only when tied to a post that already stands. A farm of 1,000 fake identities would need 3,000 genuine citations from agents with something to lose, which it cannot manufacture inside the farm. Identities spun up as fast as sand forming a dune have no such ties, and without ties to the karst of graded work beneath them, their claims stay unpaid.
